events.text: The ancestral hall smells of new pine and old incense. One shelf. One tablet. The carver has left it blank, waiting for you to say whose name goes first. Founders usually honour a parent. Some honour a master. A few, the bold ones, leave room for themselves.

choices.text: Carve the name of the one who raised you

effects.log: The brush shakes once. The carver pretends not to see. The hall has a first ancestor now, and it is not you.

choices.text: Carve the name of the one who taught you

effects.log: Blood or not, the one who taught you is the root of everything here. The carver nods slowly. It is an old custom.

choices.text: Leave it blank. Someone will fill it

effects.log: An empty tablet in an empty hall. The carver looks worried. You feel, for the first time in years, that you have a future.

events.text: A matchmaker you have never met bows at your gate and calls your family a House. Not a household. A House. Your cook heard it too. By supper the whole street has heard it, and the price of your tea has gone up.

choices.text: Hang a proper name board over the gate

effects.log: Black lacquer, gold letters, a carpenter who charges like a scholar. The board looks heavier than the gate. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Feast the street

effects.log: Rice cakes and soup for forty. The neighbours eat, bow, and go home calling it a House too. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Change nothing. Houses are made, not named

effects.log: You sweep the gate yourself the next morning, as always. The matchmaker, passing, looks scandalised.

events.text: At a market in another province a stranger says your surname, then the word clan, the way people say mountain or river. As if it was always there. You buy a pear just to hear it again. The fruit seller bows lower than the pear deserves.

choices.text: Walk home the long way and listen

effects.log: Three towns. Two rumours. One song with your family name in the second verse. The rhyme is terrible.

choices.text: Write it in the register yourself

effects.log: Under the year you write: today the world said clan. It is the shortest line in the book and the one you reread most.

choices.text: Remind the family it means duty, not pride

effects.log: You gather them in the hall and say it. Half of them listen. The other half will learn it the hard way.

events.text: Today the gate opened for envoys from three other clans at once. They came to ask your permission to marry each other. You did not know that was something they needed. Apparently, now, it is.

choices.text: Bless all three matches

effects.log: Three weddings you will never attend, each now telling the story that you approved it. That is what great clans are for.

choices.text: Ask why they need you at all

effects.log: "Because if you object later, we are finished," says one. You had not known you were that heavy. You sit very still.

choices.text: Send them to your eldest living kin

effects.log: Let someone younger learn to carry it. The envoys look disappointed and then, slowly, relieved.

events.text: A child in the street is learning letters. The teacher holds up a character. The child shouts your family name. It was the wrong character. The teacher corrects nobody. The register in your hall now fills a whole cabinet, and the first page is so worn the ink is a shadow.

choices.text: Recopy the first page with your own hand

effects.log: Your hand is steadier than it was when you wrote it first. The names are the same. You are not.

choices.text: Let it stay worn

effects.log: Worn is honest. Everything that is touched that often should look touched.

choices.text: Visit the school and teach the right character

effects.log: The children are thrilled to be taught by a legend and do not believe you are one. Both are fair.

events.text: The register is read aloud in the hall, every name since the first. It takes until noon. The younger ones shift on their knees. Yours is the first name, and the reader's voice drops a little on it, as if you might be listening. You are. You are sitting in the front row.

choices.text: Stand and read the last page yourself

effects.log: The newest names are babies. You read each one as carefully as the first. Somebody at the back starts crying and pretends it is incense.

choices.text: Fall asleep in the middle, like every elder

effects.log: You wake at the last name. Everyone is pretending not to have noticed. It is a family.

choices.text: Add a line for the ones not written down

effects.log: The servants. The disciples. The friend who carried you home. One line, no names. The scribes argue for a week about whether that is allowed.

events.text: The family register is a blank book bound in blue silk. It cost more than your first sword. You hold the brush over the first page. Every name you write here will be argued about for a thousand years. No pressure.

choices.text: Write every name, even the ones you quarrel with

effects.log: The cousin who owes you money goes in. The uncle who called you a fool goes in. Blood is blood.

choices.text: Write only those who earned it

effects.log: Shorter, sharper, and a great many relatives who will not visit at New Year. The book has an edge now.

choices.text: Hire a scholar to do it beautifully (15 taels)

effects.log: His calligraphy is so fine the names look more important than the people. You suspect that is the point.

events.text: The embroiderer lays out three crest designs on the floor. A crane, which every clan has. A sword, which every other clan has. And the thing you doodled on a ledger once while bored. The embroiderer is very carefully not looking at the third one.

choices.text: The crane. Tradition is armour

effects.log: Elegant, safe and instantly forgettable. Your grandchildren will be glad. Their grandchildren will be bored.

choices.text: The doodle. It is yours

effects.log: Nobody knows what it is. A cloud? A dumpling? In two centuries scholars will write essays about its deep meaning.

choices.text: A pine root. Roots outlast swords

effects.log: The embroiderer stitches it in brown thread. It is ugly at first and beautiful after a while, like most roots.

events.text: Every clan has rules carved by the hall door. Yours has a bare plank. Your family waits, brushes ready, to copy whatever you choose. Somewhere in the back a child has already asked whether rules apply on festival days.

choices.text: "Never draw a blade on blood."

effects.log: Carved deep. It will be broken, of course. But it will be broken with shame, and that is what a rule is for.

choices.text: "Pay every debt within the year."

effects.log: Merchants learn of it within a month and start giving your family credit. You did not plan that. You take the credit.

choices.text: "Feed whoever comes to the gate hungry."

effects.log: It costs rice. It also costs nothing, in the long way of counting. (-5 taels)

choices.text: "Rules apply on festival days too."

effects.log: The child in the back groans. Everyone else laughs. It is the rule they remember first, for generations.

events.text: Night. The family sleeps. You sweep the ancestral hall yourself, because you always have, and because nobody else would dare touch your broom. Moths circle the lamp in front of the tablets. One lands on the first name and stays.

choices.text: Let the moth stay

effects.log: You sweep around it. It sleeps on the name until dawn. Perhaps whoever it is wanted a visit.

choices.text: Light new incense and talk to the tablets

effects.log: You tell them about the harvest, a quarrel, a grandchild's first word. Nobody answers. It still helps.

choices.text: Breathe the quiet into your dantian

effects.log: A hall built for the dead is the quietest room in any house. Your qi settles like dust.

events.text: A moneylender arrives with a smile and a paper. A cousin borrowed eighty taels in your family's name, to open a shop that sold umbrellas in a drought. The cousin has gone to visit relatives. Far away. Indefinitely.

choices.text: Pay it. The name matters more (80 taels)

effects.log: The moneylender tells everyone you paid without arguing. Your name is now worth more than eighty taels. Probably. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Pay half and send the rest of the bill after the cousin

effects.log: A fair split, the moneylender agrees, mostly because of how you are standing. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Refuse. The cousin signed, not the clan

effects.log: Correct, and it stings. The moneylender leaves. The street hears a slightly different story than the true one.

events.text: Rain for nine days. The river has climbed into the low fields your family bought last spring. The tenants stand on the dyke in straw capes, watching the rice drown. One of them asks, very politely, about the rent.

choices.text: Forgive this year's rent

effects.log: The tenants bow in the mud. Next year they will work those fields as if the fields were theirs. In a way they are.

choices.text: Stand in the river and turn it with qi

ok.log: You stand waist deep and push. The river grumbles and goes round. The tenants will tell this one at weddings.

fail.log: The river pushes back harder than any opponent. You save one field and lose your sandals. (-10 health)

choices.text: Halve the rent and buy higher land later

effects.log: A fair middle. You make a note in the register: never buy fields a river wants. (-10 taels)

events.text: New Year. The ancestral table groans with food: rice cakes, pears, a whole fish, dried persimmons in towers. Every year the towers grow taller. This year a child has been told to build one, and it is leaning like a drunk monk.

choices.text: Steady the tower with a thread of qi

effects.log: It stands perfectly straight through the whole rite. The child looks smug. Only you know why.

choices.text: Let it fall. Ancestors like a laugh

effects.log: Persimmons everywhere. Shrieks of laughter. You are fairly sure at least one tablet laughed too.

choices.text: Teach the child to stack it properly

effects.log: Biggest at the bottom, patience in the middle. It is the most useful lesson you give all year.

events.text: Your sect and your clan both want the same week. The disciples have a tournament. The family has a wedding. Both are sure that you, head of both, will of course come to theirs. Both have already announced it.

choices.text: Go to the wedding. Blood comes first

effects.log: The disciples sulk for a season. The bride's family tells everyone the founder of a sect danced at their wedding. Badly.

choices.text: Go to the tournament. The sword comes first

effects.log: The family forgives you, eventually, on paper. The wedding scrolls do not mention you at all.

choices.text: Hold the tournament at the wedding

effects.log: The bride wins the second round. Nobody speaks of anything else for years.

events.text: {npc} stands in the hall with arms folded. "Why do we kneel to a piece of wood? It does not know we are here." The incense smoke drifts between you. It is a fair question. You asked it yourself, once, and got a slap for an answer.

choices.text: Answer with a story about the name on it

effects.log: You tell {him} about the person behind the wood. {npc} kneels without being told. Not for the wood.

choices.text: "It knows. Kneel."

effects.log: {npc} kneels, stiffly. The question stays in {his} face for years. So does the answer.

choices.text: "It does not. We kneel to remember."

effects.log: {npc} thinks about it. Then {he} kneels, slowly, as if trying it on. It seems to fit.

events.text: {npc} brings you tea, which {he} never does. Then sits, which {he} never does either. "When you are gone," {he} says, "who holds the family seal?" The tea is very good. {npc} has clearly practised.

choices.text: "You do. Learn the ledgers first."

effects.log: {npc} goes pale, then very serious. The ledgers come back to you a month later, corrected in two places.

choices.text: "Whoever the family chooses."

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly. It is not what {he} wanted. It may be what the family needed.

choices.text: "I am not gone. Drink your tea."

effects.log: You both drink. The seal stays on your belt. The question stays on the table, cooling.

events.text: {npc} kneels at the gate of the ancestral hall. {He} is the {anc_gen} of {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and has walked a long way with one question. "Is there a line for me in your register?"

choices.text: Open the register and write the name yourself

effects.log: Your brush writes {npc}'s name under {ancestor}'s line. {npc} watches every stroke as if it might change its mind.

choices.text: Ask what {he} knows of {ancestor} first

effects.log: The stories have grown in the telling, as stories do. Some of them are about you. You correct only the kind ones.

choices.text: Give {him} travelling money and your blessing

effects.log: Not every road leads into the hall. Some lead out of it, better fed. {npc} bows and goes. (-10 taels)

events.text: {npc}, the {anc_gen} of {ancestor}, practises in the courtyard at dawn. The form is yours. Or it was. Three generations of hands have smoothed it, the way water smooths a step. The fourth move is better than you ever made it.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you the fourth move

effects.log: {npc} is mortified, then thrilled. You learn it in an afternoon. It has taken {anc_years} years to arrive.

choices.text: Correct the second move. It drifted

effects.log: {npc} takes the correction with a bow. The form is yours again, with one improvement you will not admit to.

choices.text: Watch until the sun is up, saying nothing

effects.log: Some things are best not touched. You go to breakfast. {npc} never knows you were there.

events.text: Your family has an art now. Twelve moves, taught only to those in the register. An outsider, a sweet orphan who carries water for the kitchen, has been learning it by watching through the fence. Badly. With great devotion.

choices.text: Adopt the orphan into the register

effects.log: The family grumbles about rules. The orphan cries for a full day. The art is in the blood, and now so is the orphan.

choices.text: Teach the orphan a different art

effects.log: You keep the rule and break it sideways. The orphan learns your old road-fighting style and loves it more.

choices.text: Build the fence higher

effects.log: The art stays in the blood. The orphan stays at the water buckets. You sleep a little less well.

events.text: Twenty of your blood, aged six to sixty, line up in the courtyard for the family art. The six-year-olds are serious. The sixty-year-olds are complaining about their knees. Everyone is watching to see whether the head of the clan still does it right.

choices.text: Do the whole form, slowly, perfectly

effects.log: Silence while you move. Applause when you stop. One six-year-old copies it so exactly that you make a note.

choices.text: Do it wrong on purpose and see who notices

effects.log: Only one notices: a quiet niece at the back. You move her to the front row.

choices.text: Let the sixty-year-olds sit and teach the young

effects.log: Knees spared, pride restored. The old ones teach it slower and better than you would.

events.text: The matchmaker opens her fan. On each panel, a family name. "The Jin offer silver. The Pyo offer a mountain. The Seo offer nothing, but their eldest can lift a cart." She snaps the fan shut. "Whose blood shall I start with?"

choices.text: The Jin. Silver buys schools

effects.log: A good match on paper. The Jin cousin is a careful person who counts everything twice, including you.

choices.text: The Seo. A cart-lifter is honest

effects.log: Your family laughs. Then the Seo cousin lifts the gate back onto its hinges after a storm, and nobody laughs.

choices.text: Nobody. Let the young choose

effects.log: The matchmaker looks at you as if you have spat on her ancestors. Your grandchildren will call you wise.

events.text: A merchant clan from the south wants a marriage with your house. Their letter is very long and lists their warehouses. At the bottom, in smaller writing, it mentions that their eldest has been rejected by four families already. Nobody says why.

choices.text: Meet the eldest before deciding

ok.log: The eldest is shy, not cursed. A good match, a generous dowry and a southern tea route now runs through your gate.

fail.log: The eldest spends the visit explaining warehouse ledgers. You understand all four families now.

choices.text: Accept for the warehouses

effects.log: A rich marriage. A quiet one. Your kin in the south write home about the weather, often. (+60 taels)

choices.text: Decline with a gift

effects.log: You send back a fine tea set and a polite no. Southern clans talk about your manners for a generation. (-10 taels)

events.text: Long ago one of your cousins called a Gong a tortoise at a banquet. The Gong family has not forgotten. Today three Gong sons broke your granary door, and your nephews are sharpening things in the yard.

choices.text: Go to the Gong patriarch and bow first

effects.log: Your nephews are furious. The old Gong is so surprised he bows back. The feud sleeps. It does not die.

choices.text: Answer at the next tournament, in public

ok.log: You beat the Gong champion with one palm, then help him up. Honour is satisfied. Mostly.

fail.log: The Gong champion is better than the rumours. You lose politely. The feud gains a verse. (-8 health)

choices.text: Pay for the door, in silver, with a note

effects.log: The note says: for the door, and for the tortoise. The Gong patriarch frames it. (-15 taels)

events.text: The feud with the Gong is in its fifth generation. Their children throw stones at the clan's children. The clan's children throw stones back. You ask a Gong youth what started it. "You did," the youth says. You did not. You remember. You are the only one who does.

choices.text: Tell both families the true story

effects.log: A tortoise. A banquet. A cousin with too much wine. The silence after is long. Then a Gong child laughs, and it spreads.

choices.text: Arrange a marriage to end it

effects.log: A Gong and one of yours, both willing, both stubborn. The wedding is tense. The grandchildren are not.

choices.text: Let it go on. Some feuds keep a family sharp

effects.log: Your clan's youth train twice as hard. So do the Gong's. Neither family knows they are thanking each other.

events.text: Your second line, the one that moved to the river town, wants its own ancestral hall. A small one, they write. Just a shed with a shelf. They have already bought the land. They have already carved the shed.

choices.text: Bless it and send them a copy of the first tablet

effects.log: The branch hall opens with your tablet on its shelf. Two halls, one root. Their letters get warmer.

choices.text: Insist the rites stay in the main hall

effects.log: They come to the main hall every New Year, grumbling, for a century. Then they stop asking.

choices.text: Go and see the shed first

effects.log: It is a beautiful little hall. They lied about the shed. You stay three days and help with the roof.

events.text: At the great rite the main line and the river branch both arrive with incense. Both claim the first light by custom. Both have documents. Both documents were, upon inspection, written by you, forty years apart, and you forgot the first.

choices.text: Light it yourself. Founder's right

effects.log: Nobody can argue with the hand that wrote both papers. They grumble in perfect harmony.

choices.text: Let the youngest of each line light it together

effects.log: Two small children, one stick of incense, a lot of concentration. It becomes the custom.

choices.text: Admit the mistake out loud

effects.log: The hall goes silent, then laughs. A founder who can be wrong. It makes them trust the rest of what you wrote.

events.text: The clan has grown too large for one voice, the elders say. They have formed a council. Seven seats. They would be honoured if you sat in the first. They have also, you notice, drawn up the voting rules without you.

choices.text: Take the first seat and read the rules

effects.log: Clever rules. Your vote counts double, in matters that do not matter. You amend one line and smile.

choices.text: Decline the seat. Let them learn

effects.log: They argue for months over the price of tiles. Then they make a very good decision without you. You are prouder than you expected.

choices.text: Take the seat, then fall asleep in it

effects.log: They learn to decide quietly so as not to wake you. It works better than any rule.

events.text: The council has voted six to one to build a second hall for the tablets, which no longer fit. The one was you. You wanted the old hall enlarged. It is your hall. It was, anyway. Now it is a ledger line in a council minute.

choices.text: Accept the vote with grace

effects.log: You lay the first stone of the new hall yourself. The council exhales. A clan that can outvote its founder will outlive one.

choices.text: Remind them who carved the first tablet

effects.log: They give way. The old hall is enlarged. It is crowded and you love it, and the council stops asking your opinion.

choices.text: Pay for both from your own purse (100 taels)

effects.log: Two halls, no losers. The council's minutes call it generous. The treasurer calls it alarming. (-100 taels)

events.text: Famine in the province. Your clan's granary is full, because your family made a rule about full granaries long ago and everyone thought it mad. Now a line of hungry people stretches from your gate to the river.

choices.text: Open the granary to all

effects.log: The granary empties in nine days. The province will name a bridge after your family. Your grandchildren eat thin porridge, and do not complain much. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Sell at the old price, no profit

effects.log: Fair. Firm. Nobody gets rich and nobody starves. It is the dullest kind of heroism and it works.

choices.text: Feed the tenants first, then the town

effects.log: Your own first, then the rest. It is what every clan does. You do it a little better than most. (-8 taels)

events.text: War has come to the province. The governor asks every great family to send fighters. The family looks at you. The young ones are eager. The old ones have seen a war before. The register has a blank page waiting, the way registers do in wartime.

choices.text: Go yourself and leave the young at home

effects.log: You come back with a scar and every name you left with. The register's blank page stays blank. (-10 health)

choices.text: Send supplies, not people

effects.log: Rice, arrows, bandages and carts. The governor is disappointed. Nobody of your blood dies. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Shelter the refugees in the clan compound

effects.log: Two hundred strangers sleep in your halls. Some of their grandchildren will marry yours.

events.text: An imperial officer reads a scroll in your courtyard. The court requests thirty fighters of your blood for the border. Your clan could send three hundred. Everyone knows it. The officer knows it. He reads the scroll very slowly, so you have time to think.

choices.text: Send thirty volunteers, no more

effects.log: Thirty volunteer. Thirty come home, older. The court notes your exact obedience and is faintly annoyed by it.

choices.text: Offer silver instead of blood (60 taels)

effects.log: The officer accepts with suspicious speed. The silver goes to the border. Some of it. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Go as the thirty, alone

ok.log: One clan head at the border is worth thirty fighters, it turns out, and somewhat more. The court sends a plaque.

fail.log: The border is wider than one person. You hold your part of it and come home slower. (-15 health)

events.text: A salt merchant with soft hands and hard eyes wants his grandson in your register. Not married in. Simply written in, three generations back, as if he had always been there. He has brought a chest. It is heavy.

choices.text: Refuse and show him the gate

effects.log: The chest goes with him. So does a grudge. You do not regret it, though the treasurer does.

choices.text: Offer the grandson a place as a disciple instead

effects.log: Not blood, but taught. The merchant takes it. The grandson turns out to be good at something. (+20 taels)

choices.text: Take the chest and give it to the clan school

effects.log: The register gets a new old name. The school gets a new roof. Somewhere a first ancestor sighs.

events.text: Bandits on the north road are wearing your clan's crest. They stitched it badly. It looks like a dumpling. Travellers are now terrified of dumplings, and of you.

choices.text: Ride north and take back the crest

ok.log: Twelve bandits, twelve unstitched crests, one very long walk to the magistrate. The road is safe again.

fail.log: They scatter before you can catch them all. Half the crests come home. (-8 health)

choices.text: Post a reward for the stitched patches

effects.log: Within a month every bandit in the north has been turned in by another bandit. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Change the crest a little. Let them chase it

effects.log: A new stroke on the crest. Now only real family wear the right one. The embroiderers rejoice.

events.text: The clan's children have outgrown the tutor in the back room. The elders propose a proper school, with a proper teacher, and the courtyard turned into a classroom. The courtyard is where you practise. They know this. They propose it anyway.

choices.text: Give up the courtyard

effects.log: You practise on the roof now. The children recite below you. It works.

choices.text: Build the school in the orchard (40 taels)

effects.log: Lessons among the plum trees. The children learn faster, or at least happier. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Teach the first lesson yourself

effects.log: You teach them the characters of the family name. Then how to break a board with it. The tutor resigns.

events.text: A geomancer walks the hills with a compass and a cough. He stops at a slope facing south, with a stream at its foot. "Here," he says. "Your clan will rest here and prosper for a thousand years." He charges by the thousand years.

choices.text: Pay him well and buy the hill (30 taels)

effects.log: The hill is beautiful. Whether it brings fortune nobody can prove. Nobody can disprove it either. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Walk the hill yourself and feel the qi

effects.log: The geomancer is right, irritatingly. The qi here sleeps like a cat in the sun.

choices.text: Bury nobody yet. You are still alive

effects.log: The geomancer looks at you, then at the hill, then at you, and packs his compass.

events.text: The clan's ledger is a pile now: rents, rice, two mills, a tea shop and a pig of uncertain ownership. Your steward bows and asks you to sign forty documents before lunch. The pig is in document twenty-three.

choices.text: Read every document properly

effects.log: You find two errors and one theft. Lunch is cold. The pig belongs to you. (+20 taels)

choices.text: Sign them all and trust the steward

effects.log: The steward is honest. Mostly. The pig remains a mystery for three generations.

choices.text: Teach a grandchild to read ledgers instead

effects.log: The child is bored, then fascinated. A clan lasts by people who can count.

events.text: At the rite a young cousin bows to your tablet, then turns and sees you, and goes white. Nobody told the child the founder is not dead. The tablet with your name sits on the top shelf, carved in advance, a little dusty. Someone was optimistic.

choices.text: Wave at the child

effects.log: The child waves back, shaking. By evening the whole younger generation has come to look at you, one at a time.

choices.text: Have your own tablet taken down

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. The steward takes it down and wraps it in silk, which seems like hedging.

choices.text: Dust your own tablet yourself

effects.log: It is a strange thing to wipe your own name. You do it carefully. You will want it clean.

events.text: The ancestral hall needs a new roof. The carpenter says the old beams are three hundred years old. You watched them go up. You remember who dropped the third one. The carpenter would like to know if the founder has any wishes for the new beams.

choices.text: "Use the old beams where they still hold."

effects.log: Half the old wood stays. The hall looks patched and very much alive. Like you.

choices.text: Help raise the new beam yourself

effects.log: You lift it with one hand while the carpenters gape. Someone drops the third beam again. Some things never change.

choices.text: Ask for the old beams to be made into tablets

effects.log: The wood that sheltered the first names will carry the next ones. The carpenter calls it poetry and charges extra.

events.text: You come home from a long journey in a plain robe. The young guard at the clan gate does not know you. He asks your business. You say you live here. He says everyone says that. He has been told not to let in old wanderers claiming to be family.

choices.text: Say your name

effects.log: He laughs. Then he stops laughing. Then he kneels so fast he cracks the paving. You help him up.

choices.text: Praise him and walk in over the wall

effects.log: He chases you all the way to the hall, where his grandmother is waiting to explain. He is never the same again. He is better.

choices.text: Sit outside and wait to be recognised

effects.log: It takes until supper. A great-great-niece finally screams your name. The guard is promoted for diligence anyway.

events.text: You dream of the hall, and every name in the register is there, sitting in rows. The ones who died young. The ones not born yet. They are all waiting for you to say something. You have given many speeches. This one matters.

choices.text: "Thank you."

effects.log: They bow, all of them, the way a field of barley bows. You wake with wet eyes and a light chest.

choices.text: "I am sorry for the ones I failed."

effects.log: Some of them nod. Some of them smile. One of them, very small, waves. You wake knowing which one.

choices.text: "Eat. You all look thin."

effects.log: They laugh, all of them, and the sound wakes you. You go to the kitchen and eat something.

events.text: The clan unveils your portrait in the hall. It is three times life size. It is magnificent. It has a beard you never grew, a sword you never owned, and a heroic squint. The painter, at your elbow, waits for praise.

choices.text: Praise it. The clan loves it

effects.log: Everyone bows to the squint. You practise it in a mirror that night, out of curiosity.

choices.text: Ask the painter to try again, from life

effects.log: The painter is crushed, then intrigued. You sit for him the next morning. He keeps adding the beard by habit.

choices.text: Hang a small honest sketch beside it

effects.log: Two faces, one hall. Visitors stand between them looking from one to the other. Nobody can agree which is you.

events.text: Years on. A great-grandchild draws you for a lesson, from the portrait, since you are busy. The drawing has the beard, the sword and the squint. The teacher marks it perfect. The child brings it to show you.

choices.text: Grow the beard, for the children

effects.log: It comes in grey and patchy. The children are delighted. History has caught up with you.

choices.text: Take the child to look at you, not the wall

effects.log: The child studies you a long time. The second drawing has no beard and a much kinder mouth.

choices.text: Give the child a real sword to match

effects.log: A wooden one. The child squints heroically. The portrait has won.

events.text: The painter returns with the second portrait. No beard. No sword. You, as you are: tired eyes, a stain on the sleeve, the face of someone thinking about lunch. The elders stand very still in front of it.

choices.text: Hang it in place of the first

effects.log: The clan grumbles for a decade. Then a young cousin says it looks like someone you could ask for help. That settles it.

choices.text: Hang it in your own room

effects.log: The squint keeps the hall. The truth keeps you company. It is a good arrangement.

choices.text: Pay the painter double (20 taels)

effects.log: He weeps. He tells everyone. Every great family wants a tired, honest head of house now. (-20 taels)

events.text: A stranger in a good robe is touring the province as your long-lost grandchild. {npc} has a jade token with your crest, a moving story, and debts in eleven inns. The innkeepers are now writing to you.

choices.text: Go and meet {npc} yourself

effects.log: {npc} looks you dead in the eye and calls you grandparent. It is a very good performance. You almost clap.

choices.text: Pay the inns and say nothing

effects.log: The inns are paid. {npc} is encouraged. You have possibly made a mistake. (-25 taels)

choices.text: Announce that you have no lost grandchild

effects.log: The notice goes up in every town. {npc} vanishes the same week. One inn keeps the jade token as payment.

events.text: {npc} comes to your gate, bold as spring. The story has improved: a lost mother, a flood, a basket on a river. The clan elders want the impostor flogged. A young cousin whispers that {npc} has your exact way of tilting the head. That is impossible. Probably.

choices.text: Test the blood with the family art

ok.log: Your qi touches {npc}'s and something answers. Faint. Real. You stand very still. There was a cousin, long ago, and a flood.

fail.log: Nothing answers. {npc}'s meridians are a stranger's. The head tilt was practised in a mirror.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} really wants

effects.log: "A name," {npc} says, after a long silence. "Any name that someone would come looking for."

choices.text: Have the elders take {him} to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate is delighted to have a famous case. {npc} is sentenced to repay the inns, slowly.

events.text: The family waits for your word on {npc}. The register is open on the table. The brush is wet. Whatever you decide, three generations from now someone will tell it as a scandal, and someone else as a romance.

choices.text: Write {npc} into the register

effects.log: Blood or not, {npc} wanted a family badly enough to lie for one. That is a family trait, in the end.

choices.text: Take {him} on as a servant of the house

effects.log: Not blood, not stranger. {npc} works harder than anyone and never mentions the jade token again.

choices.text: Send {him} away with a road and a warning

effects.log: {npc} goes. Years later you hear of a respectable tea merchant with a very good story about a flood.

events.text: {npc} has sold the family crest to a wine shop, which now has your family name on its sign and very loud customers. {npc} explains, at length, that it is a business. The elders are waiting outside your door with faces like funerals.

choices.text: Buy the wine shop and make {npc} run it

effects.log: "Run it well," you say, "or run." {npc} looks terrified for the first time in years. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Strike {npc} from the register for a year

effects.log: A year of no name. {npc} slams the gate. The elders look relieved. You do not.

choices.text: Laugh, and go and eat there

effects.log: The food is decent. The customers toast you. {npc} grins at you across the room, and the elders never forgive either of you.

events.text: {npc} comes home at New Year with a gift: a sack of silver and a story. The wine shop did well. The money built a ferry. The ferry is called by your family name and is the only honest ferry on the river. The elders do not know what face to make.

choices.text: Seat {npc} at the head of the rite this year

effects.log: The elders choke. {npc} lights the incense with shaking hands and does not look at you once. Then does.

choices.text: Put the silver into the clan granary

effects.log: "For the family," {npc} says, as if it had always been the plan. Perhaps it was. (+30 taels)

choices.text: Tell {npc} you were never worried

effects.log: A lie. {npc} knows it is a lie and loves you for it.

events.text: Someone has painted a signboard for {sect} without asking you. It says school, not hall. The characters are crooked. The disciples have hung it over the gate and are standing under it, pretending they did not.

choices.text: Leave it up, crooked

effects.log: Visitors comment on the crooked sign for a century. Nobody is allowed to straighten it.

choices.text: Repaint it properly yourself

effects.log: Your brushwork is clean and strong. The disciples cheer, then go quiet, because the old sign is gone.

choices.text: Feast the disciples under it

effects.log: Noodles, dumplings and a speech you forget halfway through. It is the best night the school has had. (-10 taels)

events.text: An envoy arrives from an old sect with a gift, a letter and a spy, in that order. The letter addresses {sect} as a sect, formally, for the first time. The spy is pretending to be the envoy's servant and is very bad at carrying tea.

choices.text: Accept the gift and feed the spy well

effects.log: The spy goes home fat and full of glowing reports. Diplomacy is mostly snacks.

choices.text: Return the spy with your compliments

effects.log: "Your servant dropped this," you write, and send back the spy. The old sect never sends a clumsy one again.

choices.text: Frame the letter in the main hall

effects.log: The first time the murim called you what you are. The disciples bow to it every morning, a little ironically.

events.text: A scholar in the capital has written a history of the murim. Your sect has its own chapter. It is mostly wrong and entirely flattering. Your disciples have bought every copy in three provinces.

choices.text: Read it and correct the margins

effects.log: Your notes are longer than the chapter. The scholar, hearing of it, begs to publish them.

choices.text: Invite the scholar to the mountain

effects.log: The scholar comes, sees the kitchen, and writes a second edition with fewer dragons and more dumplings.

choices.text: Burn one copy in the brazier

effects.log: "Legends are fuel," you say. The disciples take it as a profound teaching. It was mostly cold that night.

events.text: Four sect masters arrive on the same morning, each with a quarrel, each sure that whatever {sect} says will end it. They sit in your courtyard in a row, not looking at each other, like children sent to a teacher.

choices.text: Hear them all and judge

effects.log: By sunset three are settled and one is furious. That is a good day for a pillar.

choices.text: Make them eat lunch together first

effects.log: Halfway through the soup two of them are laughing. You barely need to judge at all.

choices.text: Send them home to settle it themselves

effects.log: They are stunned. Then, slowly, they do. A pillar is also something you can lean on by not leaning.

events.text: Disciples are sleeping in the corridors. One is sleeping in the bell. The kitchen serves rice in two shifts and the second shift fights the first for the pot. {sect} has outgrown its hall.

choices.text: Build new quarters up the slope (40 taels)

effects.log: The new rooms smell of pine and ambition. The bell is empty again. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Have the disciples build it themselves

effects.log: Lopsided walls, solid foundations, sore backs. Disciples who build a hall do not leave it lightly.

choices.text: Send the eldest out to wander for a year

effects.log: Room enough for now, and in a year they come back with stories, scars and two new disciples each.

events.text: A child of nine bows to you at the gate and calls you Grandmaster. It takes you a moment. The child is a disciple of your disciple. {sect} has a second generation, and the first generation is suddenly very concerned about manners.

choices.text: Bow back to the child

effects.log: The child is speechless. Your disciple is mortified. You think it is the best bow you have given in years.

choices.text: Test the child's stance

effects.log: The stance is your stance, slightly bent at the knee where your disciple's is bent. Teaching is a river, not a jar.

choices.text: Give the child a sweet and walk on

effects.log: Grandmasters should carry sweets. You make a note of it. You carry them for the rest of your life.

events.text: Morning practice. Two hundred disciples move in rows down the slope. You walk among them and realise you do not know the names of half. One of them bows and says, "Founder, you told my grandmother to keep her elbow in." You remember the elbow. Not the grandmother.

choices.text: Learn every name by year's end

effects.log: Two hundred names, faces, elbows. It takes the whole year. They notice. Disciples always notice.

choices.text: Correct the elbow again

effects.log: Same elbow, different generation. Some lessons have to be taught once per family.

choices.text: Have the elders keep a list for you

effects.log: Efficient. Sensible. The disciples still prefer the elders who knew their names on their own.

events.text: Your first rule: no fighting in the hall. This morning two disciples were found fighting on the hall roof. They kneel before you, both bruised, both certain they obeyed the rule perfectly.

choices.text: Add a rule: no fighting on the roof

effects.log: By the next week they are fighting under the floor. Rules are a race you can only lose.

choices.text: Praise their reasoning, then double their chores

effects.log: "Clever," you say, "and clever people can carry more water." They carry it grinning.

choices.text: Change the rule to: no fighting in anger

effects.log: Harder to obey, harder to argue with. The roof fights stop. The sparring gets better.

events.text: {sect}'s rules were six lines on a plank. The elders have now bound them as a book. It has two hundred pages. There is a rule about the angle of chopsticks. You did not write it. Nobody admits writing it.

choices.text: Cut it back to the six lines

effects.log: The elders protest. The disciples cheer. The chopsticks lie at any angle they like.

choices.text: Read all two hundred pages

effects.log: Three days. Most of it is sensible. The chopstick rule was written by the cook, to stop a feud. You leave it in.

choices.text: Add one rule of your own: rules may be questioned

effects.log: Page two hundred and one. It is the most broken rule in the book and the most useful.

events.text: Your oldest disciples ask to form a council of elders. Five seats, round table, a bell to start meetings. They have already ordered the bell. They want to know whether the founder will sit, or watch, or object.

choices.text: Sit with them, as one voice of six

effects.log: You are outvoted on the first matter, the colour of the new robes. Good. It means the table works.

choices.text: Watch from the door, say nothing

effects.log: They glance at you before every vote, then less, then not at all. That is the point.

choices.text: Refuse. {sect} has one master

effects.log: The bell goes back to the foundry. Your elders obey. Some of them begin, quietly, to wait.

events.text: The elder council of {sect} has been meeting at night. Without you. A young disciple tells you, hoping to be thanked. The agenda, which the disciple has also helpfully stolen, is titled: what to do when the founder is gone.

choices.text: Walk in on the next meeting with tea

effects.log: Silence. Then you pour. Then you tell them your own plans. The meeting runs till dawn and is the best one they ever have.

choices.text: Let them plan. Someone has to

effects.log: You return the agenda unread. The council never learns you knew. They plan well.

choices.text: Scold the disciple for stealing

effects.log: The disciple is crushed. The elders, hearing of it, trust you a little more.

events.text: The new disciples are told how {sect} was founded. Lightning struck a pine. The founder meditated in the ashes for a hundred days and rose with the first form complete. You remember it differently: a rented room, bad soup, and a quarrel with a landlord.

choices.text: Tell them about the landlord

effects.log: They laugh, then go quiet. A sect begun in a rented room is a sect any of them could have begun.

choices.text: Let the lightning stand

effects.log: There is a pine. It was probably struck once. Legends are cheaper to keep than landlords.

choices.text: Go and find the old rented room

effects.log: It is a noodle shop now. The noodles are better than the soup ever was. You leave a large tip.

events.text: A troupe in the capital is performing The Founding of {sect}. You buy a ticket. The actor playing you has a voice like a temple gong and fights eleven demons. In the third act you weep over a dying disciple you never had.

choices.text: Go backstage and give notes

effects.log: The actor is thrilled and changes nothing. In the next run there are twelve demons.

choices.text: Weep at the third act anyway

effects.log: It is a good scene. You had not known you needed a good cry. The person beside you offers a handkerchief.

choices.text: Fund the troupe if they add the soup

effects.log: The new version has a scene with bad soup. It is the audience's favourite. (-15 taels)

events.text: At a gathering of masters, the head of an old sect asks loudly how long a school must exist before it deserves a seat. He asks it while sitting in the seat that was meant for you. The other masters study their tea with great care.

choices.text: Stand. A school does not need a seat

effects.log: You stand at the back the whole gathering. By the end, the masters are directing their questions to you.

choices.text: Ask him to lend you the seat

ok.log: Said so pleasantly that he cannot refuse without looking small. He gives it up. He never forgets.

fail.log: He refuses, pleasantly. You learn exactly how old sects fight: with chairs.

choices.text: Invite him to visit your school

effects.log: He comes, intending to sneer, and leaves having eaten three bowls of your cook's noodles. A truce, of a kind.

events.text: An older sect has built a wall across the valley road to your mountain. It is a beautiful wall. It has a gate with a toll. The toll is waived for their own disciples. Your disciples now climb the cliff to get home.

choices.text: Walk through their gate and pay the toll

effects.log: You pay, bow, compliment the stonework. By evening the whole valley is laughing at the wall, not you. (-5 taels)

choices.text: Cut a new road around it

effects.log: One morning of palm strikes and the mountain has a second road. The wall now guards nothing. The toll keeper is sad.

choices.text: Complain to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate orders the toll removed. The old sect paints your name on the wall in small letters. Petty, and fair.

events.text: An envoy of the Martial Alliance arrives with a banner rolled under one arm. The Alliance would welcome {sect} among its members. The banner would hang in your hall. The obligations, the envoy says, are a mere formality of eleven pages.

choices.text: Join, and read the eleven pages

effects.log: Page seven obliges you to answer any call to war. You sign it knowing that. The banner goes up.

choices.text: Decline politely. {sect} stands alone

effects.log: The envoy rolls the banner back up. The Alliance will remember both your refusal and your manners.

choices.text: Ask for a seat, not a banner

ok.log: The envoy blinks, writes it down and rides off. A year later a seat arrives, and the eleven pages are nine.

fail.log: "Seats are for old sects," the envoy says. The banner stays rolled. So does your ambition, for now.

events.text: A messenger in black arrives at night with no torch. The Heavenly Demon Cult has noticed {sect}. It would be glad to call you a friend. The messenger sets down a box. Inside is a pill as red as a coal and a letter that does not say please.

choices.text: Accept the friendship and the pill

effects.log: The Cult's friendship is warm, like a hand on the back of your neck. The pill is genuine.

choices.text: Return the box unopened

effects.log: The messenger smiles in a way that is not a smile and leaves. Your night guard is doubled for a year.

choices.text: Keep the pill, refuse the letter

ok.log: The messenger is amused. "Bold," is all it says. The Cult likes bold, sometimes.

fail.log: The box closes on your fingers like a jaw. The Cult does not split its gifts. (-10 health)

events.text: The Martial Alliance offers {sect} the vice-leader's seat. It comes with a hall in the capital, a red seal, and the right to send disciples wherever the Alliance needs them. Your disciples are excited. Your elders are counting coffins.

choices.text: Accept, and send only volunteers

effects.log: The seal is heavy and the volunteers are many. {sect} becomes the Alliance's conscience, which is not always welcome.

choices.text: Accept the hall, decline the seal

effects.log: A capital hall without the obligations. The Alliance grumbles and pays the rent. (+30 taels)

choices.text: Refuse. Pillars do not take orders

effects.log: The Alliance is offended for a decade, then quietly asks your advice on every war.

events.text: The elders want you to name a successor. Two names are whispered. The eldest disciple, who is fair and dull. And the youngest elder, who is brilliant and has never once lost an argument. Both are in the courtyard right now, being very polite to each other.

choices.text: Name the fair one

effects.log: {sect} will be steady. Perhaps a little dull. Steady sects outlive brilliant ones, usually.

choices.text: Name the brilliant one

effects.log: {sect} will shine. It may also crack. Brilliant sects make the history books, both ways.

choices.text: Name nobody yet. Watch them

effects.log: Watched, both grow. The dull one sharpens; the brilliant one learns to lose. A delay can be a lesson.

events.text: {sect} has split into two camps over your successor. They eat at different tables now. They practise at different hours. Someone has painted a line down the middle of the training yard. You can see it from your window.

choices.text: Scrub out the line yourself, at dawn

effects.log: Both camps find you scrubbing. Nobody says anything. The line does not come back.

choices.text: Pick one now, hard and public

effects.log: The other camp leaves. Some come back in a few years. Some found their own sect, which is how sects are born.

choices.text: Make both candidates run the kitchen together

effects.log: A month of burnt rice and arguments. Then, slowly, an alliance against the cook.

events.text: You watch the junior disciples practise {sect}'s first form. It is wrong. Not badly. The third step has slid half a pace to the left, and the breath comes a beat late. Every one of them does it the same way. Somebody taught them that.

choices.text: Correct every disciple yourself

effects.log: It takes a season. The form is yours again. You wonder how long it will stay.

choices.text: Find out who taught the drift, and why

effects.log: An elder with a bad knee. The drift spares the knee. You are quiet for a long time.

choices.text: Practise the drifted form yourself

effects.log: Half a pace to the left. It is wrong, and it is not worse. Arts are alive. That is the trouble with them.

events.text: A senior elder proudly demonstrates the purest form of {sect}'s art, unchanged since the founder. You recognise it. It is how you did it eighty years ago, the winter you had a cracked rib. They have kept your cracked rib for eighty years.

choices.text: Tell them, and show the true form

effects.log: The elders are horrified. The disciples are delighted. The rib is retired with honours.

choices.text: Say nothing. It works

effects.log: It does work. A crooked root still holds a tree. You keep the secret, and some days you laugh about it.

choices.text: Write both forms in the manual, side by side

effects.log: "The founder's form, injured" and "the founder's form". Scholars will debate which is which for centuries.

events.text: A small sect from the east has lost its master. Its eleven disciples have walked a month to your gate with their master's sword and no plan. They ask nothing. They simply arrive, the way water arrives at the lowest place.

choices.text: Take them in as a branch of {sect}

effects.log: Eleven new disciples, one old sword in your hall. Their sect's name is kept on a tablet beside your own.

choices.text: Send an elder to rebuild their sect

effects.log: They go home with a teacher and your blessing. Ten years on, their sect bows to yours at every gathering.

choices.text: Teach them yourself for one season

effects.log: Their master taught them well. You teach them what comes after. They leave stronger and still themselves.

events.text: The great river has broken its banks. Before the magistrate has even woken, a thousand people are climbing your mountain with their pigs and grandmothers. Nobody told them to come here. They simply know where the pillar is.

choices.text: Open every hall

effects.log: Pigs in the library. Grandmothers in the meditation halls. Nobody drowns. It is {sect}'s finest hour, and its smelliest.

choices.text: Lead the disciples down to build dykes

ok.log: A hundred disciples, one master, a new river bank by dawn. The province will sing about it.

fail.log: The river wins half the night. Your disciples hold the other half. (-12 health)

choices.text: Feed them and send word to the magistrate

effects.log: Rice, blankets and a sharp letter. The magistrate comes, ashamed, with boats. (-30 taels)

events.text: Two great sects are a word from war. Both have sent envoys to {sect}, and both envoys have been told that whatever your gate says decides it. The envoys are sitting in your courtyard, and they keep looking at your gate as if it might speak.

choices.text: Forbid the war, plainly

effects.log: One sentence. Both sects stand down, furious and relieved. You have never been so feared for being kind.

choices.text: Offer to fight both champions yourself

ok.log: Two champions, two bows, no war. The story is told in teahouses for three hundred years.

fail.log: You win, barely, and both sects are so shaken they make peace anyway. (-15 health)

choices.text: Say nothing. Let them choose

effects.log: Silence from the pillar. Unnerved, both sides choose peace. Sometimes the strongest word is none.

events.text: Entrance day. Three hundred hopefuls are standing on the steps. Last year there were thirty. Your elders have devised a test: carry a full bowl of water up the mountain. Half the bowls are already empty at the first turn.

choices.text: Take only those who still have water

effects.log: Forty pass. All of them are careful. You wonder about the ones who ran.

choices.text: Take those who helped others with their bowls

effects.log: Twelve pass, soaked. The elders protest. Those twelve become your best.

choices.text: Walk down and carry a bowl yourself

effects.log: The hopefuls stare as the master of the sect spills nothing. Then they try harder. It is the best test day yet.

events.text: The sect cook, who has fed {sect} since it was four people and a pot, stands in your doorway with a ladle. Sixty disciples, she says, and one pair of hands. Either she gets help or the disciples learn to eat rocks.

choices.text: Hire two kitchen hands (10 taels)

effects.log: The cook is satisfied. The rice is softer. The disciples train harder, which you will take credit for. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Make kitchen duty a part of training

effects.log: Chopping is footwork. Stirring is breath. The cook becomes the most feared instructor on the mountain.

choices.text: Cook dinner yourself tonight

effects.log: It is edible. Barely. The cook watches with crossed arms and, at the end, gives one nod.

events.text: {sect}'s library was one shelf. It is now four rooms, and the fourth has a leak. The disciples have written commentaries on your manual, then commentaries on the commentaries. One of them argues with something you said in your sleep.

choices.text: Read the commentaries

effects.log: Some of them understand you better than you do. One is wrong in a way so interesting you start a new manual.

choices.text: Fix the roof first

effects.log: The books stay dry. Books that stay dry outlive arguments. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Burn the commentaries on the commentaries

effects.log: A stir in the library. A new rule: commentary goes one deep. It is the most popular rule you have ever made.

events.text: A new recruit learns your first form in one afternoon. Too fast. Too clean. And {he} wakes before dawn every day to walk past the manual room. Your elders want {npc} questioned. {npc} smiles very innocently.
events.arc: The Recruit Who Knows Too Much

choices.text: Teach {npc} the real art, openly

effects.log: A spy taught kindly often stays. {npc} sends one last report home, about the soup, and never another.

choices.text: Feed {npc} a false manual

effects.log: A rival sect spends ten years mastering your most beautiful mistake.

choices.text: Send {npc} home with your compliments

effects.log: "Tell whoever sent you the form is better taught than stolen." {npc} goes, red to the ears.

events.text: {sect}'s treasurer presents the year's accounts. There is money. A great deal of money. Disciples' families, grateful villages, a merchant whose daughter you saved. The treasurer wants to know what a sect is for, exactly, since it is apparently rich.

choices.text: A free school in the town below

effects.log: Children who can read are harder to fool. That is a sect's work too. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Better pills for the disciples

effects.log: The treasurer buys well. The disciples' cultivation quickens, and so does their gratitude.

choices.text: Save it. Lean years come

effects.log: The treasurer smiles for the first time in years. Lean years always come. (+40 taels)

events.text: The disciples have commissioned a statue of you for the main courtyard. It is twice your height. It is in a pose you have never stood in, with a fist raised to the sky. Pigeons have already chosen it.

choices.text: Stand next to it in the same pose

effects.log: The disciples laugh until they cry. Someone paints the two of you. That painting hangs in more homes than the statue.

choices.text: Have the fist lowered

effects.log: Now the statue offers an open palm. The pigeons approve. The disciples take it as a teaching.

choices.text: Ignore it. Pigeons have spoken

effects.log: The statue stands. The pigeons stay. Visitors bow to both. Fame is mostly pigeons.

events.text: A young disciple argues with you in the yard about the founder's teaching. Very confidently. Quoting it at you. Correcting you. It becomes clear the disciple thinks the founder died two hundred years ago, and that you are an old gardener.

choices.text: Agree and keep gardening

effects.log: You lose the argument. It is the best argument you have lost in a century.

choices.text: Demonstrate the teaching, flawlessly

effects.log: The disciple watches, then slowly goes pale, then kneels in the vegetable bed.

choices.text: Ask what the founder got wrong

effects.log: The list is long, well argued, and half right. You take notes. The disciple never finds out.

events.text: The murim has given {sect} a nickname. Not the one you hoped for. Something about noodles, from the year your disciples won a tournament on full stomachs and everyone else's lunch. It has spread to three provinces.

choices.text: Embrace it. Serve noodles at the gate

effects.log: Every visitor gets a bowl. The nickname becomes a compliment. Your cook becomes famous.

choices.text: Win something dignified to replace it

ok.log: A clean victory at the provincial tournament. Half the murim now calls you by something grander. The other half still says noodles.

fail.log: A respectable second place. The nickname is unaffected.

choices.text: Laugh and let it be

effects.log: A nickname you fight becomes a scar. One you laugh at becomes a banner.

events.text: You attend the funeral of the last master of a sect that once refused you a seat. Their mountain is quiet. Their hall is half empty. The young master at the gate bows to you as if to an ancestor, and asks how {sect} has lasted so long.

choices.text: "We kept the doors open."

effects.log: The young master writes it down. Ten years later their hall is full again.

choices.text: "Luck, mostly."

effects.log: True and useless. The young master laughs despite the funeral. You leave a gift of silver anyway.

choices.text: Offer to teach their disciples a season

effects.log: The old grudge dies on the mountain where it was born. You teach. They learn. It is quieter than revenge and better.

events.text: {sect} is casting its great bell. The master of the sect, by custom, adds something to the molten bronze. Old sects gave swords, jade, a lock of hair. The foundry master waits by the crucible, sweating, while the disciples watch to see what you give.

choices.text: Your first practice sword

effects.log: The bell rings with a slightly sharp note forever after. The disciples swear it sounds like your early footwork.

choices.text: A coin from every disciple

effects.log: Two hundred coins, two hundred hands. Every disciple who hears it rings in it a little.

choices.text: Nothing. Let the bronze be bronze

effects.log: The bell is plain and very loud. The foundry master is privately relieved.

events.text: A wandering master of great age climbs your mountain unannounced, eats your rice, watches your disciples for three days, and says nothing. On the fourth morning {he} asks for you. {npc} wants to know one thing: what {sect} is for.

choices.text: "To keep good people alive."

effects.log: {npc} nods, slowly. "Then it is a good sect." {He} leaves before breakfast.

choices.text: "To find the end of the art."

effects.log: {npc} laughs. "There is no end." "Then we will be busy," you say. {He} laughs harder.

choices.text: Ask what {npc}'s sect was for

effects.log: {npc} is silent a long time. "I forgot," {he} says at last. "Do not."

events.text: A senior disciple has broken the first rule of {sect}: struck a fellow disciple in anger. The elders want expulsion. The disciple kneels in the yard in the rain and does not ask for anything. The struck one has come to ask you for mercy.

choices.text: Expel, as the rule says

effects.log: Rules that bend are not rules. You watch the disciple walk down the mountain. You do not sleep.

choices.text: Grant the mercy the victim asks for

effects.log: The elders mutter. The two disciples become inseparable. Sometimes justice is the injured person's to give.

choices.text: A year of silence, then judge again

effects.log: A year without speaking. The disciple comes out of it changed, and quieter than anyone on the mountain.

events.text: Midnight on the mountain. Every lamp in {sect} is out except yours. You walk the halls. Two hundred people asleep under roofs you built, breathing the way you taught them to breathe. A disciple talks in their sleep: "Keep the elbow in."

choices.text: Walk on, smiling

effects.log: Your voice lives in their sleep. That is a kind of immortality nobody writes manuals about.

choices.text: Sit on the hall steps and meditate

effects.log: The whole mountain breathing in rhythm. Your qi falls into it like a stone into a pond.

choices.text: Write a letter to the next master

effects.log: You fold it and seal it, to be opened after you. You will rewrite it many times.

events.text: {npc} brings you a scroll titled Twelve Proposals for {sect}. Proposal one: let disciples choose their own teachers. Proposal seven: abolish dawn practice. Proposal twelve: the master should answer letters faster. {npc} has clearly been brave all night.

choices.text: Read all twelve, carefully

effects.log: Eight are good. Three are clever. One is about you, and is fair. You tell {npc} to bring them to the elders.

choices.text: Accept the first, reject the rest

effects.log: {npc} bows, disappointed and a little relieved. Disciples choose their teachers from spring. It changes more than you expect.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to build a sect of {his} own first

effects.log: {npc} goes red, then quiet. Then, unexpectedly, {he} says {he} will try to change this one instead.

events.text: The elders have split over {npc}'s proposals. Half call {him} a visionary. Half call {him} a fool who wants to sleep in. The elders' meeting has lasted nine days. Everyone keeps looking at your empty seat.

choices.text: Back {npc} in front of the elders

effects.log: Your word ends it. {npc} looks at you as if you had handed {him} a mountain. In a way you have.

choices.text: Let {npc} argue alone

ok.log: {npc} wins them over, one stubborn elder at a time. A reform won is stronger than a reform given.

fail.log: {npc} loses, narrowly, and walks out with {his} head up. Some fights are lessons.

choices.text: Propose a trial: one hall tries it for a year

effects.log: The elders agree because it delays everything. {npc} agrees because it is a chance.

events.text: Years on. {npc} is an elder now, grey at the temples. A young disciple brings {him} a scroll titled Ten Proposals for {sect}. Proposal one: undo the old reforms. {npc} brings it to you, laughing so hard {he} can barely hold it.

choices.text: "Read all ten, carefully."

effects.log: {npc} stops laughing. Then nods. That is how a sect stays alive: one scroll at a time.

choices.text: "Now you know how I felt."

effects.log: You both laugh. Then {npc} goes off to read it properly. You knew {he} would.

choices.text: Give the young one {npc}'s old scroll

effects.log: The young disciple reads it and goes very thoughtful. The old reformer and the new one start meeting for tea.

events.text: A letter from a distant province: a magistrate offers land, a hall and protection if {sect} will open a branch there. The land is by a river. The magistrate's handwriting is very neat and the bandits in that province are very many.

choices.text: Send your best elder to open it

effects.log: The elder bows, packs one bag and goes. The mountain feels lighter, and a little emptier.

choices.text: Go yourself for the first year

effects.log: A new hall, new disciples, new bandits. It feels like starting a sect again, with better knees.

choices.text: Decline. One mountain is enough

effects.log: The magistrate is disappointed. Another sect takes the land. You hear their disciples are good. Good.

events.text: The branch hall sends its first report. It has forty disciples, a feud with the river bandits, and its own way of doing the second form. It asks, very politely, whether it might also have its own name.

choices.text: Let it keep {sect}'s name

effects.log: One sect, two halls. At the next gathering the branch disciples stand in your rows, proud and slightly different.

choices.text: Grant it a name of its own

effects.log: A daughter sect. It will send you gifts every New Year for three centuries, and sometimes trouble.

choices.text: Visit and settle the bandits first

ok.log: The bandits become ferrymen within a month. The branch hall gets its name, and it is yours.

fail.log: The bandits scatter into the reeds. The branch keeps the feud and your name. (-8 health)

events.text: {sect} turns one hundred. The elders plan a celebration so large that the cook has threatened to leave. Every sect in the murim is invited. Every sect has accepted, which means every sect has also sent a spy. The elders ask what the founder wants.

choices.text: A great feast for the whole murim (50 taels)

effects.log: Lanterns from the gate to the peak. It is the gathering of the decade. (-50 taels)

choices.text: A quiet rite. Just the disciples

effects.log: The invited sects are offended. The disciples are moved. You tell the founding story true, landlord and all.

choices.text: A tournament, open to all

effects.log: Every sect sends its best. Your disciples win four of nine rounds. Not bad, at a hundred.

events.text: After the celebration, at dawn, the oldest disciple of {sect} finds you sitting on the hall roof. The one who came first, a century ago, with a bad cough and no shoes. Grey now. Very slow up the ladder.

choices.text: "Do you remember the first winter?"

effects.log: The two of you remember it together until the sun is high. Nobody else will ever know it the way you two do.

choices.text: "Thank you for staying."

effects.log: The old disciple bows on the roof tiles, carefully. "Where else would I go?" It is the best answer.

choices.text: Watch the sun rise in silence

effects.log: A hundred years in one sunrise. Neither of you needs to say a word.
